text:
maria: Heads up — after rolling nvidia-driver 550.12 to eu-west-gpu-autoscale pool we have ~12 nodes failing to finish boot (stuck at initramfs / DKMS timeout). noticed this ~10m after the rollout started.

ajay: Can you paste the dkms/journal snippet? which kernel versions are affected?

maria: Most affected are the older xanadu-image AMIs with kernel `5.15.0-1129` (custom backports). snippet:```
Jun 22 03:14:21 host dkms: ERROR: Module build for 'nvidia-550.12' failed.
Jun 22 03:14:22 host systemd[1]: dkms.service: Unit entered failed state.
Jun 22 03:14:22 host systemd[1]: initramfs-tools: update-initramfs failed, boot hang.
```

kevin: Impact looks concentrated to A100-backed instances and a couple of RTX6000 legacy nodes. dkms errors show long compile times and then timeout: `/usr/sbin/dkms build -m nvidia -v 550.12 --no-debs` timing out. GPU driver module missing -> kernel panics on modules load.

jordana: Could be the gcc/kernel headers mismatch on those AMIs. Also saw a Secure Boot vs module-signing warning on 3 hosts — if SB is enabled DKMS won't install unsigned modules. but most of these hosts have SB disabled.

sre-oncall: Immediate mitigation: paused rollout, cordon the remaining 130 nodes in eu-west pool and rollback driver on one failed host to 535 to confirm recovery path. Can we prebuild modules and push as init-ramfs?

maria: Tried booting one failed host with the older 535 package (apt repo) — kernel boots clean and nvidia module loads. Quick remediation is rollback to 535 for pending hosts and rebuild AMI with prebuilt 550 modules for later try.

ajay: Two action items: 1) collect full `/var/lib/dkms/*/build/make.log` from failed hosts, 2) check if our provisioner pipeline uses `dkms` with a short `--timeout` somewhere. I suspect systemd service has a low restart limit.

kevin: Also saw NCCL warnings when one node partially came up (can't attach GPU): `NCCL WARN Timeout` — probably from missing/partial module state. This will cause distributed training jobs to fail quickly. We need to throttle scheduling and mark affected AZ as degraded.

maria: I ran `kubectl cordon gpu-node-xx` + `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` on the worst offenders. Starting a staged rollback via our deploy pipeline (rollback job triggered). deploy-bot: Rollback job queued.

deploy-bot: Automated update: rollback-to-driver-535.86 in eu-west pool STARTED (job id: rb-2024-1774). Estimated runtime 22m.

nvidia-support: Case opened with NVIDIA (case #INC-987654). They asked for full `dkms` logs, `uname -a`, `modinfo nvidia` output. Preliminary: 550 introduced a new build step that is slower on kernels without certain backports; recommend prebuilt dkms packages or using the .run installer that includes precompiled modules.

jordana: Longer term: we should avoid DKMS builds at first boot for large fleets. Option A: bake drivers into AMI (prebuild for common kernels). Option B: add a provisioner step to increase DKMS build timeout and parallelism. Option C: roll to 550 but only on nodes with kernel >= 6.x where module builds are fast.

sre-oncall: Capacity impact — we've cordoned ~12 nodes (roughly 9% of eu-west GPU capacity). Evicted 18 pods (mostly training). Need to either burst to other regions or delay non-prod jobs. Cost tradeoff: migrate training to on-demand in other regions (expensive) vs keep degraded performance here. Thoughts?

maria: For now we will: 1) finish rollback, 2) schedule an AMI bake with precompiled 550 kernel modules for kernel 5.15 and 6.1, 3) gate 550 to canary label `gpu-v2` only. I'll open a follow-up doc in #eng-infra with AMI bake steps.

ajay: For the bake, include build matrix: kernels [5.15.0-1129, 5.15.0-1140, 6.1.0-24], gcc versions [9,11], and run `dkms status` smoke tests. Also add a systemd probe that delays node ready until module load succeeds.

kevin: Also add a fallback in our smart routing to send critical workloads to dedicated capacity if driver upgrade reduces available nodes < 90%. Would avoid customer-facing incidents.

nvidia-support: Follow-up: NVIDIA provided a hotpatch (550.12.1) that addresses a DKMS build race on older kernels. They recommend testing hotpatch on a non-prod canary image.

jordana: Good. Plan: Test 550.12.1 on one canary ASG tomorrow 03:00 UTC, bake new AMI if green, otherwise keep 535 pinned and trigger replacement for the rest. I'll add to oncall runbook: steps to disable DKMS at first-boot and use preinstalled `.deb`.

sre-oncall: Logged incident in status page (notified customers with degraded capacity in eu-west). Will update once rollback finishes.

maria: Thanks everyone — rolling status: rollback in progress, canary planned for 03:00 UTC, AMI bake + prebuild queue created. I'll post the full make.log bundle in this thread once collected. :white_check_mark:

kevin: One last note — set retention of `/var/lib/dkms/make.log` to 7d for easier debug (many are rotated out).

maria: +1. Adding to infra runbook.
